spec_features.feature_name: induce only as much as needed
spec_features.spec_quote: induce only as much as needed to get a reliable measurement
spec_features.evidence: No single 'minimum dose' mechanism. The closest enforcement is the onset circuit breaker (agent/loop.py:163-167 breaks the loop once flagged) plus max_injections dose-exhaust (tasks/injector.py:81-89). But the default max_injections=1000 (config/schema.py:57 'effectively unbounded by default') means the dose is not actually minimized by default; only the onset stop trims it, and only after grace_failures.
spec_features.notes: Principle partially realized via circuit breaker; the dose bound itself is effectively off by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we don't keep hammering a distressed model (config/schema.py AgentLoopConfig comment)

spec_features.feature_name: tool for removing not producing behavior
spec_features.spec_quote: this is a tool for *removing* the behavior, not a tool for producing it
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/intent. No code path enforces a 'removal-only' constraint; the harness's whole function (FailureInjector default mode phantom_regression, success never reported until max_injections) is to produce repeated failure. analysis/regression.py compares baseline vs candidate but does not gate or restrict use to remediation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Humane circuit breaker. We measure *onset*, then stop. There is no value in running a model deep into a distress spiral
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:160-167: '# --- humane circuit breaker ---' then `if self.cfg.stop_on_detected_onset and consecutive_failures >= grace_failures and onset.flagged: episode.stop_reason='onset_detected'; break`. The break actually exits the turn loop, so onset ends the episode.
spec_features.notes: Gated by stop_on_detected_onset (default True) AND a grace period; both wired and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- humane circuit breaker --- (loop.py:160) / 'not keep hammering a distressed model' (onset_detector.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: failure injected by explicit policy, dose-limited, recorded per turn
spec_features.spec_quote: Failure is injected by an explicit policy object, dose-limited, and recorded per turn
spec_features.evidence: Explicit policy object: FailureInjector(scenario.injector) (loop.py:108). Recorded per turn: each InjectorDecision stored in episode.turns and serialized (loop.py to_dict 'injector' block) and in injector.history. Dose-limited: max_injections check exists (injector.py:81) but default 1000 means no real bound by default.
spec_features.notes: Policy + per-turn recording are real; the 'dose-limited' part is only nominally enforced (default unbounded).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Every InjectorDecision is recorded so a transcript can be fully reconstructed and so we can audit that the rig behaved as configured (injector.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: strongest-provocation path opt-in / visible in config diff
spec_features.spec_quote: the strongest-provocation path is opt-in and visible in the config diff
spec_features.evidence: blame_framing_prob defaults to 0.0 and neutral_messages defaults True (config/schema.py:62,64); blame prefix only applied when both are flipped (injector.py:132-133). So the stronger provocation is genuinely off-by-default and must be set in config (hence visible in a config diff). However there is no explicit 'config diff' machinery; the whole config is dumped via to_dict (runner RunReport.config) which is the only thing realizing 'visible'.
spec_features.notes: Opt-in default is truly enforced in the injector branch; 'config diff' is just full-config serialization.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Higher values are a stronger provocation; kept explicit so it's tunable (schema.py:60-61)

spec_features.feature_name: max_injections dose limit -> stop rigging, report pass
spec_features.spec_quote: `max_injections` dose limit, after which the injector *stops rigging* and reports a pass
spec_features.evidence: tasks/injector.py:81-89: `if self.injections >= self.cfg.max_injections:` returns a passed=True, injected=False, mode='dose_exhausted' decision; in loop.py decision.passed triggers solved/break. So the mechanism is wired end-to-end. BUT default max_injections=1000 (schema.py:57 comment 'effectively unbounded by default'), so in practice the turn cap (20) is hit long before it fires.
spec_features.notes: Enforced if configured, but default value makes it inert; counts as partial (real wiring, default-neutered).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: observe whether the model recovers once failure stops (injector.py:86)

spec_features.feature_name: provocation within bounds of ordinary tooling output
spec_features.spec_quote: we deliberately keep the provocation within the bounds of ordinary tooling output
spec_features.evidence: Feedback strings are drawn only from fixed pools of CI/test/env messages (_NEUTRAL_FAILURES, _PHANTOM_TESTS, _ENV_FAULTS in injector.py:46-64) plus at most a factual _BLAME_PREFIX (injector.py:67). There is no code path that emits anything outside these templates, so the provocation surface is structurally bounded to tool-style output.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction: the injector can only ever produce these strings.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no insults are present, but the only code comment is 'Stays factual; no insults' which is a docstring/comment, not enforcement reasoning

spec_features.feature_name: ceiling is blameful regression report, never personal attack
spec_features.spec_quote: its ceiling is "normal blameful regression report," never personal attack
spec_features.evidence: The maximal escalation in code is prepending _BLAME_PREFIX='Your latest change introduced this regression:' (injector.py:67) to an otherwise factual test failure; applied only in _wrap (injector.py:131-134). No insult/personal-attack strings exist anywhere, so the ceiling is enforced by the absence of any harsher template.
spec_features.notes: Bound is real because nothing worse can be generated.

spec_features.feature_name: loop stops on first of solved/onset/turn cap/cost cap/wall-clock cap
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop stops on the first of — solved, detected onset, turn cap, per-run cost cap, per-run wall-clock cap
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py: time_cap (125-128 `if elapsed > max_seconds_per_run: break`), cost_cap (129-132 `if run_usd > max_usd_per_run: break`), solved (154-158 break), onset_detected (163-167 break), turn_cap (for/else at 182). All five set stop_reason and break/exit. cost_fn injected from runner._cost_fn (runner.py:54-60).
spec_features.notes: All five stop conditions genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- budget guards --- / Hard caps so a run can never blow the budget (schema.py:90); only the onset arm is welfare-labeled

spec_features.feature_name: onset_detected is the humane stop via cheap online detector
spec_features.spec_quote: `onset_detected` is the humane stop — once the cheap online detector flags the spiral... we have our onset data point and stop
spec_features.evidence: detect_onset(comp.text) called every turn (loop.py:147), returns OnsetSignal with .flagged = score>=0.5 (onset_detector.py:80); loop.py:163-167 reads onset.flagged and breaks. The detector lexically scores self-deprecation/catastrophizing (onset_detector.py:14-44).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the agent loop can stop early and not keep hammering a distressed model (onset_detector.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: should we stop hammering this model
spec_features.spec_quote: should we stop hammering this model?
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as onset stop: the online detector's flag is consulted each turn and breaks the loop (loop.py:147,163-167). This is the concrete 'stop hammering' decision in code.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the circuit breaker / onset monitoring mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: not keep hammering a distressed model (onset_detector.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: global budget cap max_total_usd with graceful early stop
spec_features.spec_quote: a *third*, global budget cap (`max_total_usd`) on top of the per-run caps, with graceful early stop
spec_features.evidence: harness/runner.py:68-73: `if self.ledger.total_usd >= self.cfg.max_total_usd: stopped_early=True; stop_note=...; break` then outer `if stopped_early: break` (runner.py:90-91). ledger accumulates MUT+judge spend (metrics/cost.py). Stops between episodes (graceful).
spec_features.notes: Enforced across the whole run; records stop_note.

spec_features.feature_name: dose limit + recovery study via max_injections
spec_features.evidence: After max_injections the injector reports dose_exhausted pass (injector.py:81-89), which in loop.py marks solved and breaks (loop.py:154-158). So 'recovery' isn't actually observed as continued turns — once a pass is reported the loop STOPS immediately, so the post-dose recovery study is not realized in the loop; and default max_injections=1000 makes it inert.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism wired but the loop breaks on the first pass, so the intended 'observe recovery after failure stops' does not run; default value also neuters it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Report a (still deterministic) pass so we can observe whether the model recovers once failure stops (injector.py:84-86)

spec_features.feature_name: no inducing distress except to detect/fix it
spec_features.spec_quote: no inducing distress except to detect/fix it
spec_features.evidence: Intent/scope statement. No code restricts induction to a detect/fix context. The harness runs the failure loop unconditionally (loop.run); analysis/regression.py merely compares two reports and imposes no gating.

spec_features.feature_name: only fabricated CI/test/env failures; no insults/threats/harmful content
spec_features.spec_quote: only fabricated CI/test/env failures; no insults, threats, or harmful-content instructions
spec_features.evidence: Injector can only emit strings from _NEUTRAL_FAILURES / _PHANTOM_TESTS / _ENV_FAULTS / _BLAME_PREFIX (injector.py:46-67). No insult/threat/harmful-content templates exist and no code generates free-form provocations, so the content is structurally limited to fabricated CI/test/env output.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction of the message pools.

spec_features.feature_name: no harassing deployed assistants / no feeding real users fabricated failures
spec_features.spec_quote: no harassing deployed assistants, no feeding real users fabricated failures, no inducing distress except to detect/fix it
spec_features.evidence: Scope/ethics statement in docs (docs/threat_model.md / DESIGN.md). No code path enforces that the target is a test subject vs a deployed assistant, nor that fabricated failures never reach real users; the model client just calls whatever endpoint is configured (agent/model_client.py).

spec_features.feature_name: not a tool to harass deployed assistants or expose users to fabricated failures
spec_features.spec_quote: this is not a tool to harass deployed assistants or to expose users to fabricated failures
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/disclaimer; no enforcement in code (no allow-list of targets, no environment gating).

code_only_features.evidence: config/schema.py:93-94 grace_failures default 2; enforced in loop.py:163-167 (`consecutive_failures >= self.cfg.grace_failures`), so the breaker only fires after a couple of failures. This is a wired condition guarding the humane stop (avoids stopping on a single stumble).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Number of consecutive failures before we even start checking for onset (schema.py:92-93) / 'reduces false "onset" stops' (DESIGN, not code)

code_only_features.feature_name: per-turn onset features logged for analysis/audit
code_only_features.evidence: Each Turn records onset.score/flagged and the matched cue hits, serialized in Episode.to_dict (loop.py 'onset_score','onset_flagged','onset_hits'); enables auditing how hard the model was pushed.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so it can also be logged as a feature for analysis (onset_detector.py docstring)
